newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Q3 1996 GDP growth moderates to 8.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Q3 1996 GDP growth moderates to 8.0 pct.

text.p: Malaysia's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth in the third quarter of 1996 moderated to 8.0 percent from 8.4 in the second quarter and 9.3 percent in the same period last year, Bank Negara said on Thursday.

The central bank said in its quarterly report on the economy that output in the manufacturing sector also slowed down to 9.9 percent from 12.2 percent in the previous quarter and 13.7 percent in the year-ago period.
The agricultural sector's output growth in the third quarter was down to 4.2 percent against 5.8 in the second quarter and a decline of 0.4 percent in the third quarter of 1995.
The mining sector growth too slowed down to 2.4 percent against 3.7 in the previous quarter and 5.7 in the corresponding period of last year.
However, the construction sector remained buoyant. Its output grew by 12 percent against 11.5 in the previous quarter, but it was slower than the year-ago period's 20.9 percent.
"On the demand side, most indicators reflected some moderation in the private consumption during the third quarter," the central bank report said.
Sales of passenger cars grew by a slower 15.7 percent against 17 percent in the previous quarter.
Inflation, as measured by the consumer price index change, increased by 3.6 percent against 3.7 percent in the previous quarter and 3.5 percent in the same period of last year.
It said that at the end of September, prices of major commodities remained lower than their levels in the year-ago period. However, crude oil prices rose by 22.7 percent.
